newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, quiet period to last.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, quiet period to last.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in lacklustre trade on Thursday, and analysts predicted the quiet period would continue for the next two to three weeks, with only mild price fluctuations for most issues.

"I hope we'll see some growth after the local elections (set for April 13), or if not, towards the end of the month when most companies publish their annual business results," said analyst Damir Relja of Faktor brokerage.
"But for another two weeks activity will remain scarce," he said.
Five of 12 active issues rose, four fell and three were flat. Volume fell to 4,253 from 6,858 shares, turnover was slightly higher at 2.6 million kuna, up from 2.4 million.

Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka edged down 11 kuna to 1,795, with 473 shares sold. But traders saw the bank's price drop as a temporary correction amid expectations it would soon release good profit figures for 1996.
The bank's preference stock lost 24 kuna to 961 whereas its bearer shares added 40 kuna to 800.
Another fully-listed issue, drugs firm Pliva, stayed out of the market for the first time in weeks.
Most active food processor Podravka inched up four kuna to 295 on volume of 1,691 units. It was seen fluctuating around current levels in the absence of major boosts on the market.
"It is obvious that it suits many investors to buy Podravka at such a low price," Relja said.
Top gainer was electric manufacturer Koncar, which rose 145 kuna to 1,300, selling 31 shares.
Top decliner textile firm Varteks edged down 9 kuna to 71, with 100 shares changing hands.
Hotelier Jadranturist and Laguna were flat at 300 and 1,450 kuna respectively whereas Riviera inched up five kuna to 154.
"Tourist firms will not see major growth or livelier trading before summer, before investors see how the tourist season will go," Relja said.
Confectioner Kras fell 10 kuna to 420, trading 199 shares.
Dalmatinska banka added five kuna to 405, with 937 units sold.
Varazdinska Banka, absent from the market on Thursday, signed an agreement to list its shares on Zagreb's bourse, and said it hoped the move would draw investors and lift its share price.
